summary: Enrichment template version skew causes misrouted SLA buckets and delayed reporting
summary_short: Template version skew -> SLA misrouting + reporting lag
description: Issue summary: During a bulk enrichment-template deployment on 2026-03-12, a subset of template instances applied an older template version (v12.3.1) while the controller reported v13.0.0. This created inconsistent SLA bucket assignment for routed support tickets and a ~45–90 minute delay in generated routing telemetry observed in console. Impact: internal support routing processes were misclassifying mid-priority (P2) alerts as low-priority for ~1 hour; SLA dashboards undercounted P1/P2 routing events and on-call rotations did not receive expected notifications. Environment: production cluster in us-east handling template rollout wave #7. Affected subsystems: template-service (rollout orchestration), routing-engine (SLA assignment), reporting pipeline (metrics ingestion backlog).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a staggered template rollout using the rollout-controller with parallelism=20. 2) Force a throttled DB maintenance window for 10 minutes so worker nodes re-read templates mid-rollout. 3) Observe that some workers report older template versions while controller state shows newer version. 4) Submit synthetic internal alerts and watch support routing decisions and metrics in /console/routes and /console/telemetry.
observed_behavior:
- ~12% of template-service pods served v12.3.1 after controller declared v13.0.0 final.
- Routing engine applied outdated enrichment keys, assigning tickets to default low-priority buckets.
- Reporting pipeline showed ingestion latency spike; SLA metrics for the window were underreported by ~18%.
- Slack channel #support missed automated escalations for two customers during the window.
expected_behavior: All template-service instances should converge to controller-declared version within rollout timeout (5m). Routing decisions should reflect the declared template version immediately after rollout completes, and reporting metrics should appear within normal ingestion latency (<=60s).

comments: Priya Menon (2026-03-12): Initial report after on-call noticed missing escalations. Attached dashboard with counts and rough window. Marking P1 because customer-facing alerts were affected.

Ethan Clarke (2026-03-12): Ongoing — reproduced locally with a smaller cluster. Hypothesis: controller declares new version but a subset of workers hit a transient read error during template cache refresh. Investigating template-service cache refresh path and DB transactions.

Rami Alvarez (SRE) (2026-03-13): Identified repeated 500s from template DB proxy during rollout window. Proxy logs show connection pool exhaustion coincident with maintenance cronjob. Suggest limiting parallelism on controller during DB maintenance windows.

Ethan Clarke (2026-03-13): Applying emergency rollback plan for wave #7 to force a consistent version (v12.3.1) across nodes while we fix cache refresh logic. Will coordinate with infra to stagger re-deploys.

Alex Morgan (Telemetry) (2026-03-14): Reporting pipeline backlog cleared after rollback; historical correction job replayed 2026-03-12 window and SLA counts reconciled. Need a post-deploy verification check in the rollout job to validate template hash convergence and telemetry emission.
investigation_notes: Cache refresh path in template-service does a best-effort read with exponential backoff; when DB proxy had 502s some workers never completed the refresh before being marked Ready by k8s health checks.
Rollout-controller did not currently validate per-pod template checksum post-deploy; it only checks controller state. Lack of per-pod convergence check allowed drift.
DB proxy connection pool config default (max 50) was insufficient under parallel rollout load; maintenance job reduced available connections, causing 502s.
Telemetry ingestion lag was amplified because routing-engine emitted low-priority labels and some metrics tags were filtered by downstream aggregation due to label mismatch.
Replaying data via the reporting reprocessing job corrected aggregated counts; however, alerts that should have escalated cannot be retroactively delivered.
workaround:
- Immediate: Force a coordinated rollback to the previous stable template version across all pods for wave #7; pause further rollouts until fix applied.
- Medium term: Reduce rollout parallelism during known DB maintenance windows and add a controller flag to pause rollouts on DB proxy 5xx threshold.
fix_plan: 1) Patch template-service to require successful template checksum validation before marking pod Ready (PR submitted). 2) Add per-pod convergence check to rollout-controller; surface non-converged pods in rollout summary. 3) Increase DB proxy connection pool during rollouts and add circuit-breaker to controller to throttle parallelism on 5xx spikes. 4) Add automated post-deploy telemetry check that ensures SLA routing counts are emitted within 5 minutes of rollout completion.
related_prs_notes: PR #3182 implements pre-ready checksum validation for template-service. PR #3195 adds per-pod convergence heuristics to rollout-controller. Both PRs require coordinated rollout and e2e tests against a simulated DB proxy failure.
resolution_notes: Hotfix (rollback) applied 2026-03-13 18:30 UTC; reporting backlog replayed overnight on 2026-03-13->2026-03-14. Temporary mitigation: rollout parallelism default reduced from 50 to 10 and rollout-controller now pauses if >5% pods return template fetch 5xx. Permanent fixes in progress via PRs listed above.
next_steps:
- QA: run e2e with simulated DB proxy failures and verify per-pod checksum enforcement (assigned to QA team).
- Deploy PRs in canary with telemetry gating.
- Update Runbook: add 'pause rollouts during DB maintenance' step and add verification query to Telemetry runbook.
- Follow-up postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-18 (owner: Priya Menon).
notes_for_support: Support should be aware that customer-facing escalations during the 2026-03-12 window may not be recoverable; proactively reach out to affected teams listed in the incident and provide summary of reconciliation counts after replay completes.
